inclusion: Men or women 16 to 80 years of age, inclusive, at time of assent/consent; enrollment of subjects <18 years only if acceptable per local law/regulation
Ability to provide written informed consent/assent and comply with schedule of protocol assessments
Diagnosed with UC ≥3 months prior to screening, confirmed by endoscopic and histologic evidence
Active UC confirmed by endoscopy with ≥10 cm rectal involvement; proctitis-only subjects capped at 15% of enrollment
Moderately to severely active UC defined as modified Mayo score (MMS) of 4 to 9, including endoscopic score (ES) ≥2 and rectal bleeding (RB) score ≥1

Surveillance colonoscopy within 12 months before baseline (or colonoscopy at screening) to rule out dysplasia in long-duration pancolitis/left-sided colitis; adenomatous polyps removed prior to first dose

Demonstrated inadequate response to, loss of response to, or intolerance to at least 1 conventional therapy (oral 5-ASA, corticosteroids, thiopurines) or biologic/JAK inhibitor therapy (anti-TNFα, anti-integrin, anti-IL12/23, JAK inhibitors), with adequate course per local guidelines

Permitted concomitant therapies (stable oral 5-ASA, oral corticosteroids at defined stable doses, probiotics) with specified stabilization periods; immunosuppressants (AZA/6-MP) discontinued ≥2 weeks prior to randomization
Adequate hematological function (WBC ≥3.5x10^9/L, ANC ≥1.5x10^9/L, lymphocytes ≥0.8x10^9/L, platelets ≥100x10^9/L, hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL)
Adequate hepatic function (total bilirubin ≤1.5xULN, AST/ALT ≤2.0xULN; Gilbert's syndrome allowed)

Females not of childbearing potential (postmenopausal or permanently sterilized) OR using highly effective contraception; males with partners of childbearing potential must use condoms during treatment and for 30 days after
exclusion: Severe extensive colitis (likely need for hospitalization/surgery within 12 weeks, fulminant colitis, toxic megacolon, bowel perforation, or prior colectomy)
Diagnosis of Crohn's disease, indeterminate colitis, or fistula consistent with Crohn's disease
Diagnosis of microscopic, ischemic, or infectious colitis
Hospitalization for UC exacerbation requiring IV steroids within 12 weeks of screening (single IV dose acceptable)
Positive stool pathogen assay or C. difficile toxin at screening (retest allowed after treatment)
Pregnancy, lactation, or positive β-hCG at screening
Clinically relevant neurological, endocrine, metabolic, psychiatric, cognitive impairment, or substance abuse/dependence disorder that could jeopardize subject or study interpretation

Cardiovascular risk conditions (recent MI/unstable angina/stroke/TIA/decompensated or Class III-IV heart failure, AV block, sick sinus syndrome, asystole, recurrent bradycardia/syncope, abnormal vital signs or ECG at screening/Day1, recent changes in anti-arrhythmic drugs)
FEV1 or FVC <70% predicted with FEV1/FVC <0.70 at screening
Uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c >9%) or diabetes with significant comorbidities like retinopathy
History of macular edema or retinopathy
History of active TB, untreated/inadequately treated latent TB, or active/latent TB at screening (with defined exceptions for treated latent TB)
Clinically significant active infection within specified timeframes or requiring IV medication, or infection risk that may worsen with immunosuppressive therapy
HIV/AIDS or positive HIV antibody test
Acute or chronic hepatitis B infection/positive HBV markers
Current hepatitis C infection/positive HCV markers with detectable RNA
History of opportunistic infection (e.g., PML, PJP, cryptococcal meningitis) or disseminated herpes simplex/zoster
History or current primary/secondary immunodeficiency
History of cancer within 5 years (except treated basal/squamous cell skin cancer) or colonic mucosal dysplasia
History of lymphoproliferative disorder, lymphoma, leukemia, myeloproliferative disorder, or multiple myeloma
Hypersensitivity to etrasimod, excipients, or placebo compounds
Prior treatment with S1P receptor modulators
Recent biologic (≤8 weeks) or small molecule (≤5 half-lives with detectable levels) treatment prior to randomization
Investigational therapy ≤3 months prior to randomization
Prior treatment with ≥3 biologics or ≥2 biologics plus a JAK inhibitor approved for UC
Topical rectal 5-ASA, short-chain fatty acid enemas, or steroids ≤2 weeks prior to/during screening
Topical rectal traditional medicine (e.g., Chinese medicine), herb enemas, or suppositories ≤2 weeks prior to randomization
Methotrexate ≤8 weeks, or cyclosporine/tacrolimus/sirolimus/MMF ≤16 weeks prior to/during screening
Live vaccine receipt ≤4 weeks prior to randomization
Previous treatment with natalizumab
Previous treatment with lymphocyte-depleting therapies (e.g., alemtuzumab, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, etc.)
Previous treatment with D-penicillamine, thalidomide, dimethyl fumarate, or pyrimidine synthesis inhibitors
IV immune globulin or plasmapheresis ≤3 months prior to randomization
Chronic use of moderate/strong CYP2C8/2C9 inhibitors/inducers or UGT1A7 inhibitors ≤4 weeks prior to randomization

consent_versions.summary: Initial protocol version establishing the Phase 3 etrasimod UC induction study design, eligibility, and assessments.

Provided additional guidance for Day 1 post-dose cardiac monitoring procedures based on FDA feedback, including revised postdose vital signs, 12-lead ECG timing, monitoring of subjects not meeting discharge criteria, and new discontinuation rules for cardiovascular symptomatic events.
Region-specific amendment; specific content of changes not detailed in the available summary-of-changes documentation.

Updated eligibility criteria (contraception requirements, hematological function thresholds, ALT/AST limits), added ophthalmoscopy/OCT and TB screening safety guidance, removed prohibition of concomitant QT-prolonging drugs based on QT study results, and added a 4-Week Safety Follow-Up visit.
Region-specific amendment; specific content of changes not detailed in the available summary-of-changes documentation.

Added guidance for virtual/offsite study visits, added anti-arrhythmic drug restrictions to prohibited concomitant therapies, clarified timing of screening OCT/PFT assessments, added a new exclusion criterion for topical rectal traditional medicine/enemas/suppositories prior to randomization, and refined several eligibility criteria (e.g., cardiovascular exclusion criteria, hospitalization timing) for clarity and safety.
